title: sparse-prefill-policy-tiler-and-compact-quant-profiles
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Production workloads with a high proportion of short, single-turn requests were paying a disproportionate cost for cold KV-prefill and heavyweight quant profiles. This PR introduces a lightweight 'policy tiler' that slices prefill/caching policies into sparse, size-bounded tiles and a companion set of compact quant profiles targeted for short-context workloads. Goals: 1) reduce startup token overhead for small requests, 2) lower memory and compute penalties from loading full-size quant kernels for latency-sensitive paths, 3) provide a simple opt-in mapping from traffic class -> prefill+quant profile. What this PR does: - Adds a policy tiler component to the serving-config layer that splits existing prefill rules into tiled fragments (sparse-prefill) and exposes a tile selector based on request size, latency budget, and recent cache hit rate. - Introduces three compact quant profiles (q-lite, q-compact, q-hybrid) tuned for 1-128 token generation budgets. Each profile trades off kernel memory and token throughput to favor lower latency and reduced GPU memory pressure. - Adds a runtime mapping so customers can pin traffic classes in their config: e.g. "small-chat" -> sparse-prefill + q-lite. - Exposes a /admin/cost-mapper endpoint (read-only by default) that shows per-tenant cost-estimates for active policies to aid engineering rollouts. - Includes a simulator harness for quick offline validation of tile size vs cold-start token cost. Migration notes: default behavior unchanged unless a policy mapping is applied; the policy tiler is behind a feature flag (feature_prefill_tiler) and defaults to off in Dedicated/Private by config to avoid accidental cost shifts. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal canaries (10% traffic), followed by customer opt-in via console templates. Checklist: - [x] implementation and unit tests - [x] integration tests for cache semantics - [x] simulator harness and sample workloads - [x] docs for console + API mapping - [x] perf benchmarks against baseline - [x] add admin read-only endpoint - [x] feature flag gating for Dedicated/Private - [ ] post-rollout cost telemetry job (follow-up).
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial service skeleton and API (tiler service + selector), compact quant profile definitions and build hooks, simulator harness and unit tests, admin cost-mapper endpoint, docs and examples, fixes following CI/flaky test reports.
files_changed: serving/tiler/service.go - new policy tiler and selector
serving/tiler/tiler_test.go - unit tests and property checks
review_comments: Liam: Please add a doc paragraph on safety of tiled KV-caching; worried about increased cache churn. Author: Added a churn guard and documented eviction heuristics in docs and tests. Priya: Can q-lite be automatically selected for streaming responses? Comment: Added selector hook and unit tests. Diego: Integration test flaky on CI (race in simulator harness); identified missing wait in test harness. Author: fixed by adding deterministic seeds and explicit sync. Final: approvals from Liam and Priya; Diego requested small nits that were addressed. CI initially failed lint (missing gofmt) and one flaky sim test; re-ran and all checks passed.
benchmarks_summary: Local+internal canary results vs baseline (main): 1) median P95 tail latency for 1-32 token requests reduced by ~18% (down from 44ms to 36ms) with q-lite + sparse-prefill; 2) cold-start token overhead reduced by 40% for short requests in the simulator (measured as fewer KV prefill tokens emitted); 3) GPU memory usage decreased ~6% on pooled hosts when q-compact selected for middling workloads; throughput for long-form workloads unchanged due to profile mapping rules. Microbenchmarks included end-to-end latency, kernel init time, KV prefill bytes, and token cost estimates per request.
release_notes: Introduce optional 'prefill policy tiler' and three compact quant profiles (q-lite, q-compact, q-hybrid). Feature is behind a feature flag and must be enabled per-tenant. Adds read-only admin endpoint for cost mapping. This is non-breaking and disabled by default.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash via web UI after approvals. Merge commit message summarized policy tiler design, mapping syntax, and canary rollout steps. Changelog entry added.
test_plan: Unit/integration tests included. Manual canary: enable feature_prefill_tiler for internal canaries (10%), exercise short-chat and long-chat templates, run cost-mapper to verify expected delta, monitor P95 and cache hit-rate dashboards for 24h. If cache churn > +5% or cost per token increases for small requests, roll back the flag.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary (10%) with internal smoke tests 2) Gradually increase to 30% over 48h while monitoring: cache hit-rate, P95 short-request latency, and per-tenant cost estimate. 3) Expose mapping templates in Console under "single-turn optimization" with opt-in toggle. 4) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, promote profiles to recommended templates. Backout: disable feature_prefill_tiler and revert mapping template.
notes_for_backports: No ABI changes; for maintenance releases include only the compact quant profiles and admin endpoint with feature flag turned off. Backport to 1.24.x should skip simulator harness.
additional_context: This PR is intended to complement (not replace) the larger batching/caching autotuning work. The tiler focuses on conservative, size-bounded changes that customers can opt into per-traffic class. Follow-ups planned: automated telemetry-based policy recommendations and a cost-aware profiler that suggests tile sizes for specific tenant workloads.
